utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, kindly call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today is Wednesday, 25th of November, 2009. Let me first greet the accused, the witness, the Defence counsel, Mr. Bos, Mr. Scott, and their case manager, and all the people assisting us. You have an IC number for us, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. The Petkovic Defence have submitted their objections to documents tendered by the Prosecution for admission through Witness Bozo Pavlovic. This list shall be given Exhibit number IC01128. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Let me use these few moments to thank the usher. He's told us that he's leaving us as of next week for a new job, and I want to express my sincere thanks for his very good work, done in the interests of everybody, whilst he was working as an usher in this Trial Chamber. On my behalf, on behalf of my colleagues, I wish him the best in his new job, and I note that once again the best are leaving, one after the other. I'm rather worried about it. Who's going to be the next one out? Whatever the case, I really thank you, Mr. Usher. I wish you all the best in your new job. Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody and Your Honours. Your Honour, if I may join on behalf of the Defence also with our deepest respect and wishes for a new success on the new job to our usher. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kovacic. Mr. Karnavas, I believe -- yes, you had something to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. I'll take 30 seconds, approximately. On November 19th, the Trial Chamber issued a decision concerning certain videos, and based on that decision we now have some rather very clear guidance from the Trial Chamber which we, unfortunately, didn't have prior to that because we were relying on the standards that -- or the way the Prosecution had introduced its videos or similar-type evidence. Based on that, we would like to have the opportunity to go to HTV and actually get the necessary criteria, or at least make the attempt to do so, as far as dates, times, with precision, and then have another opportunity for you to consider that evidence. And as I understand it, we have seven days to file for reconsideration. Given the task that is involved, we would need a little more time. We would ask that we be given until December the 7th, that would be a week from this Monday, to have all that arranged with the Croatian government, to go to the HTV, to get the documentation hopefully with a notarised statement documenting with precision the dates and what have you where all these interviews -- television interviews took place. So that would be my request. And, of course, we would have no objections if the Prosecution wanted to seek similar leave for its evidence as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, do you have any observations?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to you, Mr. President, all those in and around the courtroom. In fact, the Prosecution filed a motion yesterday seeking exactly that relief. We've tendered some additional video material, or we tendering video material with initial information to hopefully satisfy the Chamber's requirements. So, indeed, consistent -- anticipating Mr. Karnavas' position, we have filed our motion yesterday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After discussing the matter, the Trial Chamber grants this dead-line until the 7th of December to the Defence, by which date they will be able to file their submissions. We are going to continue with the cross-examination by Mr. Bos. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and good morning to everyone in the courtroom. Good morning, Witness. Your Honours, I would like to start in private session for the first part of cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that the parallel of executive authorities of the HVO were set up in Konjic and Jablanica municipality around May/June 1992 and that Mr. Dragutin Peric became the president of the HVO Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June, the president of the HVO of Konjic, that position was transferred to Ivica Azimovic, and Dragutin Peric was the president of the HDZ of Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Be that as it may, it's correct that there was an executive HVO authority set up in Konjic in June 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just have one remark. I believe that the Prosecutor has gone beyond the limits of the direct examination with this question. I, personally, am not opposed to your allowing him to ask this question, but I want to point out that this goes beyond the scope of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It goes without saying, Ms. Alaburic, these Judges are professional judges. They are not sleeping here at the hearing. They are listening. They know exactly what is going on, unless you think that they are brainless, and then, of course, your objection would be legitimate. Please pursue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. This wasn't the point of my remark. But if I should ask for a redirect, I wanted to point out that this goes beyond the scope of the examination-in-chief. That's the only reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the Prosecutor put an important question to you. You probably don't really see the reasons behind the question, but he said the following: The HVO set up a parallel authority. You rectified, saying that Dragutin Peric was the president of the HDZ, and you mentioned Ivica Azimovic, who was president of the municipality, but I don't think that the problem stems from this. The problem comes from the words used by the Prosecutor, a "parallel authority." Now, there might have been a parallel authority, but I would like to know, as far as you're concerned, whether it is because the Muslims didn't want to share authority with the HVO, because of this the HVO decided to set up a parallel authority, or whether Muslims wanted the HVO to join in with them, but it was the HVO who turned them down. You see, it's a complex situation, and in both cases, whatever the case may be, you know, this might have repercussions on other parameters. Now, of course, you knew what was going on at the time because you were there, so could you tell us exactly what this parallel authority was all about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, the HVO, that is, the structures of power of the HVO, wanted to protect the interests of the Croatian members of the armed forces, that is, the Territorial Defence at the time. They wanted to protect the interests of Croatian soldiers and the Croatian people in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But could you tell us why this protection could not have occurred within a joint authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was such a mixed instance in which there was a dis-balance in some things and the taking of some decisions. If that had continued, we would have lost our function, and clearly somebody had to protect the Croats who at the time were members of the units that had defended the Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you correctly, the HVO, on its own, decided to set up a parallel structure in order to defend the interests of the Croats.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If somebody is threatened, then they must somehow see to it that their interests are defended at that moment, so we were fighting for our interests at that moment in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just some follow-up questions on this. You said that there was a dis-balance in the authority that existed at the time. Now, I think at that time there was a war presidency --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. General Praljak had a problem? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a technical question. It's been the second day already. In order to understand you, when you speak French, and then the response, we have to switch between channels. My patience has come to an end. I'm losing half of what is being said. I do ask you that in the following break, you see to it that a technician come and fix this, because this is a disgrace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Registrar will do what needs to be done, and let's keep our fingers crossed and hope it will be solved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said that there was an imbalance in the political authority that existed in Konjic at the time, and we're talking about May/June 1992. Now, at that time there was a war presidency, and isn't it correct that the Muslims and Croats were equally represented in this war presidency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were, initially. In April and May, there was equal representation, and the decision-making was made on that basis. But as I said yesterday, there was later out-voting, and the direction of combat activity was no longer what had been agreed upon, but everything was moving into the direction that the members of the Muslim ethnicity wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we're talking about May/June 1992. I think at that time you were allies and were co-operating quite well against -- you know, in your fight against the Serbs. Didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And I said yesterday, with regard to the liberation of the communication towards Sarajevo, that the liberation of the village of Bradina was a demand put forward exclusively by Muslim representatives. But in order to avoid problems, we took part in that action and conducted it together with the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it not true that the real reason why the HVO set up a parallel executive authority in Konjic was because Konjic was to become part of the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, even though the existing authorities were working fine and it was very unlikely that the Muslims would ever hand over control to the Croats in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it wasn't like that at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to another topic. Sir, is it correct that after the HVO authorities were established in Konjic that -- and also in Jablanica, that every person in the municipality that wanted to travel in the area of Herceg-Bosna, that they needed a pass with a stamp that was issued by an HVO authority in order to travel through the territory of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: These passes that you mention, I know that in the early days, in April and May, they were issued by the Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence. They issued permits for travel throughout Herzegovina and even for going to Croatia. After that, once the HVO had been established, for crossing some check-points controlled by the HVO, such a permit was needed. And as for check-points controlled by ABiH members, you needed a permit to pass there. I personally had a pass issued by the Territorial Defence to pass the check-points controlled by ABiH members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could I ask you to take a look at Exhibit P581, P00581. It's at the beginning of the binder, Witness. It's, I think, the -- it's the second document in the binder. P00581, Witness, is a document dated 15 October 1992, and it's a signed order from the Stjepan Herceg Brigade commander, Sagolj, referring to all people, persons in the territory of Konjic and Jablanica to have their freedom of movement passes authenticated. Now, have a read through this document, and then after you've read it, I would also ask you to look at P00582, which is also related to this document. Does P00581 confirm what we just said, that -- what I just asked you, that if people needed to travel through the territory of Herceg-Bosna, and that they needed an HVO pass, and that that pass had to be signed by the Stjepan Herceg Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order by Zdravko Sagolj saying that only the stamp of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade is acknowledged on such passes, which means that passes issued in the battalions to soldiers from those battalions who wanted to visit their families who were refugees in Croatia, and that would happen, and sometimes the battalions would issue many such passes, so -- and that detrimentally affected our combat readiness. So there weren't enough soldiers there to man a complete shift, and that's why the commander, Zdravko Sagolj, issued this order to the military police not to allow soldiers from Konjic to leave the municipality without this stamp, this brigade stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. And if we can now move to 50082 [sic] -- 00582, my apologies, and we'll see it's a document -- the next document, and it's related to the document that we just saw. And here Mr. Sagolj -- Commander Sagolj is writing a report to Mr. Boban, Mr. Prlic, Mr. Stojic, and Mr. Siljeg, informing him about the problems that you've just mentioned, and he takes a fairly firm position and he says: "I was forced, due to their failure to carry out orders, to disband the 3rd Battalion Command from the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, Konjic, as well as the HVO Municipal Staff Command, Jablanica." And then reading the last paragraph of this report, it says: "It is necessary in this situation to appoint, without delay, a new HVO Municipal Staff Command and its president, as well as other military and civilian bodies in Jablanica. We therefore kindly ask you to take appropriate action on your part so that this can be done as soon as possible." Now, sir, why do you think would Sagolj have asked for a complete replacement of the HVO military and civilian bodies in Jablanica? That's quite a dramatic thing to ask.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This doesn't refer to the whole town, only the Command of the 3rd Battalion. And if you remember well, the 3rd Jablanica Battalion belonged to our brigade, that is the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, and it can be seen that they weren't acting in accordance with the commander's instructions and they continued to issue such passes stamped by the battalion so that members of HVO from Jablanica were able to go to Croatia and so affect the combat readiness of the battalion. So since they had refused the first order, the commander, Zdravko Sagolj, saw himself forced to replace the command which didn't carry out his orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, sir, doesn't it go further than just the military part, because it also says to replace the civilian HVO bodies in Jablanica, which makes sense, because the document is also addressed to Mr. Jadranko Prlic?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, objection. Could the Prosecutor please point out to us where mention is made in this document of replacing the civilian authorities at Jablanica, because I admit I cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, if you read the last paragraph, it says: "If necessary in this situation, to appoint, without due delay, a new HVO Municipal Staff Command and its president, as well as other military and civilian bodies in Jablanica." So there is a reference here to civilian bodies, and the fact that the report is addressed to Jadranko Prlic, who was -- it seems to me that that would insinuate that it was also -- relates to civilian bodies; doesn't it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to draw everybody's attention that the entire document shows that people should be replaced in the Municipal Staff of the HVO, and the Municipal Staff of the HVO was the military part of the HVO which was transformed into a brigade about that time. And the part that concerns the military and civilian bodies, as the sentence goes on, is the appointment of totally new people, not the replacement of the old people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since we have interrupted, I believe that the witness has not been given enough time. The witness has not been given enough time, and I don't see a reason why we should persist in avoiding the penultimate paragraph which clearly explains the whole document. We have been playing games. We are putting questions which imply things, and the penultimate paragraph, just like in the last document, provides a very clear answer to all the questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I object to these ongoing interventions. These are the same sort of things that have been going on now for some weeks. It's completely inappropriate. There's no point and no proper purpose for counsel to get up, make speeches, argue their case in front of the witness, clue the witness in to where they're going, the answers that the witness should give. There are absolutely no reasons for these interventions. The Prosecution is going to increasingly be on its feet to object to it as many times as it takes. This is improper, it's a waste of time, in a case that is already taking a great deal of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. My objection was clear. It was: Give the witness the time. And the Prosecutor is purposely putting the questions constructing and discussing various paragraphs in that document, meaning the witness is following those questions, without giving him a proper time to read the document. That is my point, only this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Excuse me, Your Honour, but that's never been the practice for the last three and a half years. Unfortunately, because of the limitations of time, there is rarely -- there is rarely the opportunity to have a witness read an entire document while he's sitting in the courtroom. That's nothing new. I don't think we're inventing new rules for the first time, three and a half years after trial. If Mr. Bos is being accused of misleading the witness and he's acting unethically, then let counsel give support for that. Otherwise, counsel should remain seated. If Ms. Alaburic wants to raise issues for clarification on redirect, of course, and use her time that way, of course, that's her prerogative, if the Chamber thinks it's appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If I may, just this point, Your Honour. It was always the rule, always, whenever the witness was dealing with a short document, that the witness was provided time to see the document, to understand the context of the document. I agree when it was multi-page documents, then probably it wasn't possible. But this is a short document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I observe, Mr. Scott appears to be saying that it's been the practice in this court over the last three and a half years not to give the witness the proper time to read the document. Now, that does happen from time to time, but we must reserve the right not just to jump up every time an entire document has not been read - of course we accept that, that would be wasteful - but we must reserve the right to observe when it really is necessary, in fairness to the witness, for him to answer the questions, that he should have proper time. And if there is a practice -- if there has been a practice that witnesses do not have proper time, then that practice needs changing immediately, because evidence should not be given on the basis that a witness does not have proper time to look at the document before he answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I think by this time we could really end this discussion. The witness has had the time to read the document 10 times in the meantime during these discussions. Please continue, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have had time to read the document during these exchanges by the parties. Mr. Bos is putting a question to you. He wants to know why there was a change in the HVO Municipal Staff Command, both at the military level and at civilian level, among other things, in Jablanica. He's asking you this question because, well, he has a reason for asking it. You may not be aware of the Prosecutor's reasons, but the Judges have been sitting here for several years, and as soon as asks a question, the Judges put the question into its proper context of the case. Based on this, you're supposed to answer the question, but when you do, you must be aware of the context, which may elude you, but you must know the contents of the document. Look at the third paragraph. It looks as if there were changes because of what is said in this third paragraph. And as I understood your previous answers, you explained what the problem was about. So there are two possibilities. One is that the change was connected to major political reasons; namely, the taking over of HVO for ideological or other reasons, and then people are replaced. Second possibility, a take-over that is going to take place by changing officials, but that is linked to other technical reasons; for instance, the fact that stamps are going to be used, that steps are going to be taken that have nothing to do, meaning that there's a need for adjustment. So what is your answer? Did it happen for ideological reasons, why the HVO changed people, or was it to meet specific local circumstances which resulted from individual behaviour and that had to be adjusted ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I was very clear when presenting my position. The 3rd Battalion, despite the order issued by Commander Sagolj, did not act upon his order as issued. In other words, they continued to use the stamp of the 3rd Battalion, and they continued to use the stamp of the Municipal HVO Council of Jablanica when issuing certificates to the members of the unit who were going to Croatia, and this had a huge affect on the combat readiness in Jablanica. That's why he says that he is going to remove the commander of the 3rd Battalion and replace him, and then he goes on to propose the replacement of the civilian structures in Jablanica municipality. And this is just a proposal. He's not the one doing things. He's just proposing that they should be done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me put it to you that Commander Sagolj asked for their replacement because he considered that the local HVO authorities in Jablanica were too weak to pursue the goals of the Croatian community. If I put that to you, what do you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is not correct. We saw in the previous document that our commander, Zdravko Sagolj, put a ban on using the stamp on those certificates that did not hail from the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, so also certificates issued by the battalions could not be used and were not valid if members of the brigade were going to Croatia for family visits and for other reasons, because such departures had a negative effect on the combat readiness of the brigade. Despite all that, despite him being very clear about all that, the 3rd Battalion went against his order. They went on to willfully certify such certificate with the stamp, and so did the Municipal Council of Jablanica. That's why he says in this document that he's going to replace Mijat Tomic, the Jablanica Battalion commander. And he also requested for the responsible civilian structures in the territory of Jablanica to be removed and replaced. And all that was the result of the disobedience of those structures which concerned the visits of the members of those units to their family members who were refugees in Croatia, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Let's move to another topic. Besides the military information that you received through your position in the army, what kind of public information sources were available in Konjic at the time in 1992 and early 1993? Was there television, was there radio, were there newspapers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Radio Konjic. We couldn't watch TV because the repeater which was giving the TV signal was in the hands of the JNA and it was switched off. There was no transmission in Konjic. Radio Konjic was in the hands of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A little while ago, you said that you would also receive media reports. What kind of media reports would you receive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that this was done by Radio Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, while we were listening to you, one could get the impression that you were perfectly isolated. The television relay was in the hands of the Serbs, and maybe it broadcasted TV Belgrade. Radio Konjic was held by the Muslims, so are you saying that there was no Croatian media to broadcast information? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, your fellow citizens living in Jablanica or Konjic probably had radio sets; 1993 is not the Middle Ages. And on these radio sets you can obtain Radio Zagreb, or was it not possible to get that radio on a radio set?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jablanica could receive signals from Radio Zagreb and others because the repeater existed for their transmission. I was talking only about Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What about Konjic? Wasn't there even one person that had a radio set that could listen to Radio Zagreb on the shortwave radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose so. I wouldn't know. I was a member of the military, and I was always on missions in the field, and I often found myself in the areas where there was not even electricity as a result of the previous shelling which destroyed the entire electrical network at the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in the last few days there's been some talks about this Constitutional Court decision declaring the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna illegal. That decision was rendered on 18 September 1992. Did you learn about this decision when you were in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's no need to look at a document. I think it was on Monday that there has been a reference to the Constitutional Court decision in Sarajevo about a decision in which they rendered -- in which they declared the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna illegal. Do you remember that, there was talk about this decision?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that decision was rendered on 18 September 1992, and my question is: Did you learn about that decision at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that decision. However, that decision was rendered only by the representatives of the Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you learn about that decision?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I heard about the decision on Radio Konjic. All the decisions that came from Sarajevo were broadcast on Radio Konjic. And also I heard that at our political information briefings in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, in October 1992, there were armed clashes between the HVO and the ABiH in Prozor. Now, in light of your function, I take it that you would have received some information about what went on between the Muslims and Croats in your neighbouring municipality. What did you learn about this conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only then that I was appointed that function. I believe that at that time I was attending military intelligence training in Medjugorje just about that time, so I did not know much about the developments in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you may have been in training, but I take it that when you came back, you must have heard what went on, because it had quite an affect on the region, what happened there. Are you telling me that you don't know anything about what happened in Prozor in October?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard, but I wouldn't be able to discuss any details. I did hear about conflicts in Prozor, of course I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me quote from a UN report that was -- from a Mazowiecki UN report, these were UN observers who were in the region, and they reported about these events in Prozor in the following way, and I'm quoting from Exhibit P01462, and I'll just read out to you what is said in this report: "There are accounts of ethnic cleansing being carried out by Croat forces in the area of Prozor towards the end of 1992. Clashes between Muslim and Croats forces resulted in as many as 3.000 Muslims fleeing into the mountains in October 1992. There are reports of large-scale arbitrary detention of Muslim men, women, and children by Croat forces. Muslim detainees were also reportedly asked to sign an oath of allegiance to the Croat authorities. It is estimated that 60 to 80 Muslim homes were destroyed in Prozor even after combat had stopped. Non-violent attempts by Muslim residents to return to the town after the fighting were reportedly blocked by Croats. The freedom of movement of those Muslims who remained in Prozor has reportedly been severely restricted." Now, sir, this is a UN report about the situation. Did any of the information that I just read out, did you receive any of this information as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the situation in Prozor later, but as I said, I don't know what initiated those conflicts in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, the Trial Chamber has heard evidence that thousands of Muslims -- Muslim refugees from Prozor were moving to the neighbouring municipalities, including Konjic; it was Jablanica, Bugojno, but also Konjic. Is it correct that Muslim refugees were moving into Konjic around November -- late October, early November 1992 from Prozor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Refugees from Prozor did not arrive in Konjic. Maybe they ended up in the outskirts, where our 1st Battalion was, but they did not arrive in Konjic as such. Most were accommodated in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we have a report which says that there were about 912 Muslims arriving in the village of Kruscica in Konjic municipality. Does that ring a bell if I give you that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just said that this is one part of Konjic bordering on Prozor where our 1st Bojna was. It's part of the outskirts. There were no refugees in Konjic, itself, which was under the control of our 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you refer to Konjic, itself, you refer to Konjic town; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I said that when it comes to Konjic municipality, they arrived only in the villages which were closer to Prozor, and that applies to that village of Kruscica, which is very near Prozor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to January 1993. Now, sir, is it correct that armed clashes between the HVO and ABiH broke out in Gornji Vakuf in January 1993? What can you tell us about that conflict? What did you learn about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear much. I only know that conflicts broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was the HVO in Konjic in any way involved in the operations in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's have a look at another exhibit, which is P01153.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a small question for you, Witness, but I'm going to put it in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's 10.30, so maybe a good time for the break.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we had left off at Gornji Vakuf. And I had asked you whether you thought that the HVO in Konjic was in any way involved in Gornji Vakuf, and you said you didn't think so. Can you have a look at P01153. I don't know if you have it in front of you or not, but this is a report dated the 15th of January, 1993, from Brigadier Petkovic, and it's an order of Brigadier Petkovic to the HVO in Prozor, Gornji Vakuf, Bugojno, and Konjic. Now, as to what he orders to the municipality of Konjic, it can be read in the third paragraph. He says: "Block all communication and roads towards --"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one? Which number?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apologies. P01153. Witness, I think you're too far -- you're too far down in the binder. It's about the sixth document in the binder. Maybe the usher can help you find it. P01153. So, in fact, you have the document right in front of you. So I was saying so this is an order from Brigadier Petkovic addressed to the HVO in Prozor, Gornji Vakuf, Bugojno, and Konjic. And as far as Konjic is concerned, he orders Konjic to block all communications and roads towards Prozor and Vakuf. Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object to lack of precision. This is not an order. This is an instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well, an instruction. It does read "an instruction for further procedure."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall that such instructions were received from Mr. Petkovic on the 15th of January, 1993, to the HVO in Konjic, that you had to block all communications and roads towards Prozor and Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know this document. If anyone got it, then probably the unit commander. And I don't think that there were any obstacles or barricades or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as you're concerned, the HVO Konjic was not at all involved in any operations relating to Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's have a look at another document, which is P01911, and this is an ECMM report dated the 16th of April, 1993. Now, sir, I'm going to refer extensively to this document, but for now I'm going to just stick with the first two paragraphs of this report, and then later on I'll deal with a couple of other parts of this report. But for now, I would like you to look at Chapter 1, which is called "General Background," and I'm going to read out to you the first two paragraphs of this report: "In January 1993, violent clashes broke out between HVO and BiH forces in the Gornji Vakuf region. The cause of the conflict was initially unclear, yet the fact that forces external to the region were involved suggested something out of the ordinary." "At the time, military commanders from the HVO (Colonel Siljeg) stated that they were on the verge of a major military victory and no one was going to stop them. Indeed, only days before the ECMM secured a cease-fire, the mayor of Siroki was televised on the hills surrounding Gornji Vakuf, urging on his troops to take the town. The HVO clearly wanted control of this town." Now, sir, is it not true that around January 1993, the HVO attacked Gornji Vakuf with the aim of taking military control over this municipality, in the same way as they had done with Prozor two months earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really unable to comment this, because I was a member of a unit that never went outside Konjic. I have no information about this, and I didn't know about these events when they went on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it not true that these HVO military actions in Prozor and Gornji Vakuf caused great anxiety amongst the Muslims in the neighbouring villages of Konjic and Jablanica, and also Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area where I was, no such anxiety could be felt either in the Croatian or the Muslim members at Konjic, because the events were far removed from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you say "far removed from Konjic," but aren't Prozor and Gornji Vakuf neighbouring municipalities of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prozor is, but Gornji Vakuf is more removed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you to show -- let me ask you to look at another document, which is a Defence exhibit which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. You know that when there's a document shown, I always look at it very carefully. I'm not just obsessed with what the Defence or the Prosecution -- the case that they're trying to put. But I checked the document, and I note there's a paragraph called "Regional Importance" on this document. It's right after the "General Background" chapter, and he mentions Prozor, Jablanica, Konjic. There is mention also of the Vance-Owen Plan, of Provinces 8 and 10, but what I'm interested in is what comes after that. It says that the reasons for all this is quite clear; it's the electrical power for Herceg Bosnia and -- comes from this area because there's a number of dams and so forth and so on in that area. The international community, represented by the person writing this report, is giving a strategic, economic, and financial reason for these military actions. It seems that it has to do with electrical power and to know who exactly is going to be in control of the electrical generation facility. So you were in that area, so you knew about this. Do you think that this matter of electrical power was essential for this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree with that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. At the time early in January, could you tell us who was in control of the electrical power generation facilities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At Jablanica, it was controlled by persons of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to check this with you because it might be important later on. Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you to look at Exhibit 4D01591, 4D01591. 4D01591.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the last document in the folder, in the binder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an intelligence report from Mr. Branko Kvesic to Mate Boban, dated the 11th of March, 1993, and I'd like you to look at this document in relation to the first two paragraphs of this report. And maybe I'll just read out the paragraphs: "We have reliable intelligence that in February this year, in Konjic municipality, at the proposal of Muslim organisations, MOOK was formed and that a number of meetings were held where the political situation in this and neighbouring municipalities was discussed. At this organisation initiative, a number of meetings were held with HVO representatives where it was stressed that they did not recognise HVO civilian authorities, dubbing them 'para-government' and 'para-civilian authorities.'" Let me just ask you about this first paragraph. Did you know about this organisation, what's called MOOK, and their views on what was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know their name, but I knew of the existence of these Muslim organisations, which certainly had different positions from the local Muslims. They were more extreme, and they took such decisions, because you can see further down who was a member of that organisation. Nezim Halilovic is mentioned, and so it becomes clear why they decided not to co-operate with the Croats. And we spoke a lot about Nezim Halilovic yesterday. If you forgot it, let me repeat that it was the mufti who led the Muderiz formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that, Witness. Let me read out the second paragraph of this document as well: "On 27 February this year, at the proposal of religious officials, an extended meeting of Croatian and Muslim intellectuals was held. At the meeting, Nusret Secibovic (SDA) and Halil Gagula (representative of Muslim intellectuals) stated that they did not recognise the HVO government or the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna policies." Now comes the following sentence, which says: "The incidents in Prozor and Gornji Vakuf were brought up, and it was stressed that the situation in Konjic could not be seen in isolation." Now, sir, would you agree with me that here we see very clearly a link about the events Prozor and Gornji Vakuf and the effect it had on the municipality of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there was no close link, but that the intellectuals of Konjic municipality wanted to set up such a link so they could deny the Croatian people in the Konjic municipality and react to some events that had happened or were happening outside our municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, is it your evidence that the Muslims in Konjic not at all felt threatened about what was going on in their neighbouring municipalities of Prozor and Gornji Vakuf, that the Muslim population in Konjic did not feel threatened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I know, because nothing happened on the territory of Konjic municipality, and the local conflicts up there had been stopped, and there was no need for anybody to feel fear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But something did happen in Jablanica, didn't it, because in the beginning of today's session we saw a report that you drafted in which you said that the situation in Jablanica was becoming more complex and that a conflict could begin at any moment? You remember saying that in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I also said that the displaced persons from Prozor had come to Jablanica and that there had been provocations, such as throwing explosive devices at the premises of the 3rd Battalion and the guards guarding it. And as far as Konjic is concerned, except for these three villages that were closer to Prozor, there weren't any displaced persons, and so no tensions arose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, despite the HVO threat coming from Prozor and Gornji Vakuf, is it not true that the ABiH 4th Corps was still trying to avoid, at any cost, of getting into an armed conflict with the HVO in January 1993? Maybe in order to clarify what I just said here, have a look at Exhibit 4D00421 in the binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we follow you, Prosecutor, I still want to examine this document. As I said already, this is a very complex case, and the more documents we see, as far as I can see, the more complicated it gets. Some time ago earlier on today, you spoke about Dragutin Peric, and then you mentioned the name of the HVO presidents, and I wondered why you made a distinction between the HDZ and the HVO. But I didn't put any question to you because it wasn't quite clear to me. And I now discover this document, in which it is written clearly that there are problems between the HVO and the HDZ. Until today, through a set of documents, I believed then those who were in the HVO, be it in the military structure or in the civilian structure of it, were basically all HDZ members and that there was, therefore, no difference, no distinction. And I now see this document which indicates that there is a problem between the HVO and the HDZ. And by looking further into this document, Witness, I realise, upon reading it, that the HVO represents possibly a political municipal entity or possibly even a military one, whilst the HDZ is the political movement. And since there are differences in opinion at the level of the Konjic municipality, but it may be so elsewhere, too - I don't know - the author of the document seizes Mate Boban of the issue in person in order to try and find a solution to the problem, because it is said that the dissensions between the HDZ and the HVO in that time may have catastrophic consequences for the Croat population in Konjic. You were there in that municipality. Did you experience differences in the way the political party, the HDZ, assessed the situation and the way the HVO authority saw it? Did you experience that, as seems to transpire from this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Konjic was a special case, in that the president of the HDZ was not also the president of the HVO, because a president of the HDZ, at the time when it was clear that there would be a conflict between the JNA and the members of the Serbian people, at that time Dragutin Peric did not engage in preparations for the defence of the Croatian people, but, on the contrary, left Konjic with his family, and Ivan Azinovic took over the role of coordinator. And once the situation calmed down to some extent, when Dragutin Peric returned to Konjic municipality, problems arose, because he, as president of the HDZ, logically should have been the representative of the HVO too. So we -- when I say "we," I'm not referring to myself, but the other persons in the Croatian leadership, as it were, proposed Ivan Azinovic and logically elected him president of the HVO of the Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your view, when you're an HVO member, you automatically must have your membership in the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not necessarily. I was a member of the HVO, but didn't belong to any political organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were a member of the HVO, but you were not an HDZ member. But if I understand properly, those who hold positions of responsibility had better be HDZ and HVO members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's for every individual to decide, whether they want to belong to a political party or not. I personally considered it unnecessary for me to join a political party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you to look at Exhibit 4D00421. This is an exhibit that you have seen also, I think, on Monday or Tuesday. It's a Defence exhibit. And I'd like you to read -- I'll read out to you paragraph 3 of this decision -- of this document. It's an order by Mr. Pasalic dated the 14th of January, 1993. And paragraph 3 of this order, which is -- and the order is addressed to various brigades, including the brigades in Konjic and Jablanica. Paragraph 3 reads: "Avoid conflicts with the HVO at any cost, regardless of the attempts of extremist factions doing everything to ensure that the relations between Muslims and Croats deteriorate. Only in the case of an armed conflict against members of the BiH armed forces should there be an equally energetic response, meaning that fire-arms should be used. This relates especially to the situation around Jablanica and Konjic, where all forces of the ABiH are to be put into full combat readiness and HVO forces are to be prevented from taking over Jablanica and Konjic and from establishing their own authorities." Sir, isn't it correct that here the ABiH in Konjic and Jablanica were prepared for defensive actions, as they expected an HVO attack on their territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it says. But if we remember the documents that we went through yesterday, we were able to read that defence positions are to be taken until orders are given for subsequent attack actions. They want to avoid conflicts, they say, but there weren't any conflicts at the time. There were minor provocations, but they raised their combat readiness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at another document, which is 4 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. Witness, this is a document that mentions extremist factions. This is not the first time we hear about this. There are many documents from both sides, from the ABiH and from the HVO. And here it is very clear. Mr. Pasalic, he may be lying, I don't know. I'm just reading what is written. He says that there are extremist factions and that this could be so that the relations between Muslims and Croats could deteriorate. This is not the first document I see about this, and the impression is that on both sides, on the Croat and the Muslim sides, there are agreements between both, but there are individuals that play a game that is such that it causes incidents. This is what Pasalic says, but we have similar documents to this effect by the HVO. You were on the ground. Did you experience this type of situation in which the relations with the Muslims were good - it may be that you went to school together, you knew each other very well - and then there are other individuals who are really in muddy waters, playing dubious games - we don't know what for - and they cause problems? This is what the document seems to say. Do you agree with Mr. Pasalic or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday I said that Pasalic had in mind the extremists who were members of the BiH Army units. I said yesterday that during that period of time, refugees and displaced persons came from Eastern Bosnia, from the direction of Mount Igman, and that they were more extreme than the locals. I also said yesterday that we could co-operate with the locals, and we manned the defence lines facing the Serbs together with them, without any problem whatsoever, or at least for a while, until the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could I ask you to look at 4D00374. 4D00374. This is an order dated 19 January 1993, and it's an order by Halilovic, addressed to the Command of the 4th Corps and the Konjic Municipal Defence Staff. Now, what I would like you to look at is paragraph 2, and I'll read it out. It says, paragraph 2: "BiH Army units in the area of Jablanica and Konjic should be at full combat readiness and prepared for persistent defence in case of an attack." Now, sir, isn't it very clear in this document that the HVO in Konjic and Jablanica were expecting an attack of -- well, that the ABiH in Konjic and Jablanica were expecting an HVO attack on their territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I am repeating that most reports referred to defence at the beginning. Later on, they referred to attacks. And in this case, the activities are geared towards defence. I don't see the danger for the HVO, in the territory of Jablanica and Konjic, to attack members of the BH Army. We know that in Jablanica, there was just one battalion of the Croatian Defence Council which had about 150 men, so what kind of danger could there have been in Jablanica? What threat was there for them in Jablanica at the time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I'll tell you what threat was coming. I'm not talking about maybe the local units within Konjic and Jablanica, but I'm talking about units from Prozor and from Gornji Vakuf who were causing a threat to ABiH units in Konjic and Jablanica. It was not only the local HVO unit, but also units from outside the territory that were threatening the territory of Konjic and Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see a threat coming from Prozor. All the conflicts in Prozor and Vakuf had already stopped, and there were no concentrations of HVO members in the territories of Prozor and Vakuf, which means that there were no soldiers in any large concentrations there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at one other Defence exhibit, which is 4D00433. Now, sir, this is a document dated the 20th of January, and this is an order by Brigadier Petkovic, addressed to the Konjic HVO. And it reads: "Establish contact with the BiH Army in Konjic and work on calming down the situation." "We have information that the Chetniks are planning to enter and take control of Konjic." Now, sir, isn't it correct that the information of a potential Serb attack on Konjic may have prevented the HVO from attacking Konjic in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We discussed this document yesterday. It says here that Juka's units, which were deployed on Mount Igman, were engaged with the BiH Army, and they, themselves, were members of the BH Army. The Zulfikar Brigade, much more extreme than Juka's brigade, expelled that brigade and incarcerated them in Ovcari. Then they were released, and they came and joined our brigade. There were some tensions as a result of us taking them on. General Milivoj Petkovic ordered that the brigade should be moved from Konjic Brigade to avoid any possible conflicts, because at that moment we needed co-operation, as we had intelligence that an attack was being prepared against Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a minor correction. On page 49, line 7, the witness said "more extreme."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did you know that around this same period of time, we're talking here about mid-January 1993, that the HVO authorities issued orders to the effect that the ABiH units in a number of municipalities, including Konjic and Jablanica, were to submit their commands to the HVO Main Staff? It's been referred to in this case as the ultimatum orders. Have you heard about these orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I didn't know that the BH Army was supposed to subordinate itself to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's have a look at P01139.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Juka's men, we're talking about Juka or Zuka Prazina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Juka Prazina, and Zuka is Zulfikar Alispago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The unit that was there, who did it belong to, the HVO or to the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Juka's unit belonged to the BiH Army, and throughout 1992 it was deployed on Mount Igman, and it controlled entrance into Sarajevo. Once the Zulfikar Brigade was established, Zulfikar wanted to move that unit because for some reason that brigade -- unit did not suit him. In any case, both units belonged to the BiH Army. Zulfikar Alispago and his men engaged in an armed conflict with members of Juka's unit, and they disarmed that unit and they expelled that unit from Mount Igman. Then they transferred them to the territory of Konjic municipality, or to be more precise, they were incarcerated in Ovcari. Whether somebody released them from prison or whether they fled, I don't know. In any case, they came to us and sought our protection. We accepted them, we received them. And in order to avoid any misunderstandings, we didn't want our members of the BiH Army who were in Konjic to hold that against us and to start saying that we were cooperating with the enemy. General Milivoj Petkovic ordered for that unit to be moved from Konjic in order to avoid any conflicts, any discords, any misunderstandings with the BiH Army in Konjic. This was, indeed, done, and we forwarded that brigade in the direction of Mostar. Actually, some units of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As to members of Zulfikar Alispago's brigade, were -- they were Muslims, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We spoke quite extensively about them yesterday, and the Zulfikar unit that was established on Mount Igman and was acting in conquering the territories that we were talking about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are telling us that this unit got into conflict with the unit headed by Juka Prazina, that it was taken in by the HVO, and that General Petkovic ordered for that unit to be moved to Mostar. Did I understand you properly? And if so, does this mean that by the 20th of January, 1993, the HVO could have some form of military authority over a fighting unit that had belonged to the BH Army and that may have still been part of it, but that did not agree with Prazina, and that therefore the HVO had some degree of control over that unit? Is that how the situation was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that there has been a misunderstanding. This is what I said. I believe there has been a misunderstanding. Maybe you did not understand me properly. I said that that brigade -- actually, Juka Prazina's unit conflicted with Zulfikar Alispago's brigade. Both of them were members of the BiH Army. Zulfikar Alispago and his unit disarmed Juka Prazina's unit and chased it away from Mount Igman. Some of Juka Prazina's troops were incarcerated in Ovcari, near Konjic. I don't know whether they fled from the prison, whether they were released by somebody. I wouldn't know that. However, during the night they arrived in the command of our brigade to seek our protection. They wanted our side to protect them or to allow them to join us. We kept them maybe for a day, maybe 24 hours, and there were already objections on the part of the BiH Army which was deployed in Konjic and on the part of the entire 4th Corps. In order to avoid any tensions mounting in this territory, which was the territory of Konjic municipality, General Milivoj Petkovic ordered men from that unit, not the entire unit, but just men who had arrived and applied to become members of our brigade, headed by Juka Prazina, to move from the municipality Konjic sector, and we transferred them in the direction of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To your knowledge -- I mean, what you're saying is very clear. I have nothing to say about it. Later on, what command did Prazina's unit remain? Was it part of the HVO, or did it return to the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When they arrived in Mostar, I believe that they joined the HVO units there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you tell us that then they joined the HVO units. In other words, after January there were Muslims who joined the HVO. Do I understand properly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is an exception. It is only about those men who had been in conflict with Zulfikar Alispago and the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, we have heard many times that in the HVO there were a number, sometimes considerable, of Muslim soldiers. Did the reverse also happen? Were there members of Catholic faith and Croat origin in the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Could it then be that members of Juka's unit who joined the HVO were such Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, was Zulfikar Alispago a Croat or a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zulfikar Alispago was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Juka Prazina, was he a Muslim or a Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Had you heard of a colonel called Siber who was a Croat and he was in the ABiH army?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just an intervention. In the interpretation, we heard the word "Siljeg," and I understand you mentioned a person called Siber. I am just saying this to avoid any misunderstandings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Had you heard of a Croat who was a colonel and called Siber, S-i-b-e-r, who was in the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've heard of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you look at Exhibit P01139. You have to move back in the binder. P01139. Okay, I think you have it. Sir, this is an order dated the 15th of January, 1993, and it's an order from Brigadier Petkovic. And I'll read out a couple of paragraphs from this order. Paragraph 1: "All units of the HVO Armed Forces and of the BiH Army in Provinces 3, 8, and 10," and Konjic and Jablanica would have fallen under Province 8, "be placed under the command of the HVO Main Headquarters, that is, under the command of the Central Bosnia, North-Western and South-Eastern Herzegovina Operative Zone." Then moving to number 4: "Members and units of the HVO Armed Forces and of the BiH Army who do not submit to the command in items 1 and 2 herein, leave the provinces where they do not belong. Otherwise, they will be treated as paramilitary units and disarmed." And then if we move to paragraph 8: "The order shall be carried out by 20 January 1993." Now, sir, were you aware that Brigadier Petkovic ordered this on 15th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this document before. I suppose my commander was informed and didn't do anything, he didn't act upon this order. No measures were taken to subordinate those units in the territory of Konjic. Nothing happened to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, I've not seen this order, I've not heard of it. Maybe my commander, the brigade commander, saw it, but he didn't do anything to act upon the order contained herein.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move again to P01911, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, a question I wanted to put to you, and I thank Mr. Bos for having shown you this document. If I understand correctly, in Konjic there was a majority of Muslims, and Konjic was located in a province which should have been controlled by whom, according to you ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we're talking about the Vance-Owen Plan, then in the province, it would be under the control of the HVO. But as I say, I have not seen this order. Maybe my commander, the brigade commander, was privy to this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I mean, you're a local, you lived there, you went to school there. You're very familiar with this area. So according to you, thinking that Konjic could eventually end up under the HVO control, was that realistic, when we know that this -- in the town and even in the municipality, there was a majority of Muslims? You even told us recently that today there are 90 per cent Muslims living in that area. So do you believe this idea was realistic? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whether it was realistic or not, I don't know. However, I know that members and representatives of the Croatian people kept on seeking agreements and arrangements with Muslims in Konjic municipality, and they never took decision in haste on their own. They negotiated until a final and official political solution could be reached for Bosnia and Herzegovina, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But is that the reason why the brigade commander, Sagolj, didn't carry out the order, because maybe he thought that it would be best to try and find an agreement rather than strictly apply an order which may seem quite unrealistic? And the brigade commander, Sagolj, might have been a man of experience. I don't know him, I've not seen him. But maybe he decided not to carry out the order and decide to find an agreement with the Muslims. What's your take on this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that Mr. Sagolj -- I can't speak on his behalf. I can't tell you anything about his meetings, negotiations. I suppose that he was in consultations with somebody from the top leadership, because he could not say on his own, I'm not going to carry out this order. I suppose that he must have received some instructions for further actions, because those enclaves were established according to a pattern, and details had to be coordinated, but the big picture was there. I believe that representatives of the Croats in Konjic did try to negotiate and agree on certain things, that they didn't want to do things on their own. They kept on insisting on negotiations and agreements in regard to any of the problems that occurred in the municipality of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the Muslim side, if they knew that in the future, with the Vance-Owen Plan, they would be in control of the province, and that the armed forces would be under their own control in a number of Muslim provinces, but when they saw that the HVO wanted to control Konjic, did they tell you about their opinion, say that it would be best to enter into a dialogue, or were you ever in contact with your Muslim counterparts, anyway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had contacts with the members of the ABiH who were working -- who were doing the same kind of work as we. We focused on the then enemy, the JNA and the Serbian side. And as far as these things are concerned, I had no contacts or communication with my colleagues from the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, although you didn't have contact with Muslim soldiers about this order, and you, in fact, didn't know about this order, would you agree with me, sir, that if Muslim soldiers would have known about this order, that it would have -- that the Muslims in -- the Muslim soldiers in Konjic would have felt a military threat in relation to this order, that they would consider this order as a military threat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know with regard to this order, some structures tried to strike some agreements, and I think that even Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic was involved in these negotiations. And with regard to -- or, rather, these agreements and this co-ordination with the Croatian people was or must have been the reason why he was replaced by his own people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm a bit puzzled by your answer, because you've stated that you didn't know about this order, and now you're saying, As far as I know with regard to this order, some structures tried to strike some agreements. Now, were you aware of this order or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say "based on this order." I said that there were people who tried to strike agreements, and among others there was Rusmir Hadzihuseinovic who spoke to us. But I didn't say "based on this order."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like to now move to another topic, which is a document that we've discussed extensively on Monday, which is 4D00454. And it's in that binder as well. These are the 20 March 1993 minutes of the joint meeting between the ABiH and the Muslim police stations. 4D00454. Now, sir, this document, as I said, it was discussed extensively. If I understood what your conclusion was about this document, it's that you interpreted this document as evidence of an offensive plan of the ABiH and the Muslim police in Konjic and Jablanica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you went through a number of these items in this order, but some other paragraphs were skipped, and some of these paragraphs is something that I want to go through with you. And it's, in fact, starting with the first operative paragraph of this protocol, as it reads, and it starts off by: "Upon analysis of the military-safety situation in the free territory of the indicated municipalities, significant deterioration of the relations between HVO and legal government authorities of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the recent period, and particularly since continued negotiations in New York began, was established. The reason thereof lie in the establishment by force of parallel authorities by HVO, which is manifested through ..." And then they are listing a number of acts that they considered as acts from the HVO parallel authority. They talk about the implementation of a taxation system. So is it correct that the HVO implemented a taxation system in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The taxation system at Konjic during the war, I don't know whether it was in existence at all and how it could have been implemented. I'm not clear about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then, the second item: "Control of the flow of goods and persons, whereby unlawful actions of bringing in owners of private shops for enforced taxation are carried out." What do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that any one private entrepreneur in the municipality of Konjic was apprehended, because I was a private entrepreneur, too. And as far as the flow of goods and persons are concerned, you have seen the check-points for traffic control in the municipality of Konjic. From Aleksin Han and Bradina, on the M-17 highway, they were all held by ABiH members. They had full control over them, and they could also enforce some sort of taxation, so they could take away goods from people. So if you're looking for a taxation system, you can now see who had the power to levy taxes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you about one more, the use of vehicle license plates of the so-called Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Was that occurring in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Konjic, there may have been a small number of such license plates that were used during the war. Most vehicles at Konjic had no license plates at all. Only the vehicles that would proceed toward Croatia or other countries did have license plates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we then continue in the document, then, in the next paragraph there's a reference to the Constitutional Court decision that we discussed earlier. And then paragraph 1 is one that I would like to -- I would like to read out. It says: "In the free territories of Jablanica, Konjic, and Hadzici municipalities, implementation of all regulations, as adopted by legal authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and all municipalities, is to be enforced." And then what follows are various measures, at least in my reading, on how these rules need to be enforced. Now, sir, didn't this document -- in this document, didn't the ABiH and the civilian police at this meeting simply agree, We are not going to allow the HVO to take control over Konjic, Jablanica, Hadzici, and from now on we're going to see to it that only the rules of the legitimate authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina are being enforced? Isn't that, in fact, what these minutes are saying? And don't you think that they also -- that they had a fair point to agree on the enforcement of the rules of the legitimate authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina rather than the rules of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, who represented, A, a Croatian minority in Konjic? And --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be better if questions were asked one at a time, we suggest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, let me then just say: Would you agree that this document simply says, We're going to follow the legitimate rules of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and in order to do so, we're implementing a number of measures? Isn't that exactly what this document says, and nothing more?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that measures must be implemented, but who took the decisions about these measures? Were the decisions made with the participation of the Croatian people, too, or only the Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me read out paragraph 7. It's one of the paragraphs that you also discussed on Monday. It says: "Defence lines towards the aggressor are to be strengthened, and full control of the area in the direction Jablanica-Kute-Here-Scipe is to be secured, and these forces are to be linked with army forces in neighbouring municipalities." Do you recall this paragraph? And is it correct that you saw this paragraph as -- well, do you recall it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall it, and I also marked these directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the map that we saw and that became an IC document is -- where we saw the lines going up were based on this paragraph. Now, sir, if you read this paragraph, doesn't it read as a defensive action rather than an offensive action? Doesn't it say defence lines towards the aggressor -- by the way, let me ask you, who is here the aggressor when they refer here to the aggressor? That would be the HVO, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Jablanica municipality, there was no JNA, and there were no Serbian aggressor, because Jablanica was removed from that line. So when they say "aggressor" here, they mean the HVO. And when they say full control in the direction Jablanica, et cetera, is to be secured, we're speaking about villages with a mixed Croatian-Muslim population. So they want to set up a communication line from Jablanica towards Kute, Here, and Scipe. There were no Serbs there, so this can refer only to the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were doing that in order to create a defence line. You know, that's what this paragraph starts with, defence lines towards the aggressor. So isn't it true that they were taking measures in order to defend themselves against HVO aggression?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In each order of theirs, we can read "take defence positions until further orders," and these orders can be aggressive or otherwise.
