And as far as I can see, it wasn't a defence action that ensued; it was an attack action. So when you enter an area, you take a defensive position, and from that you can launch offensive activities, but you can also receive an order to retreat. In this case, you have taken a defence line, established a defence line and waited for subsequent orders, and these orders were to move the forces in the directions stated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move to the armed clashes on the 23rd of March, 1993. Now, you've said that the 23 March clash was a one-sided attack of the ABiH on the HVO in Konjic, and you claim that this attack was sort of the starting point of an ABiH military offensive against the HVO, and that this attack was based on the minutes that we just looked at; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, based on these minutes that were drafted, on the 23rd of March the implementation of this agreement started, which affected our 1st Battalion with offensive actions and conflict. And in the town of Konjic, other units were blocked. We saw the report by Midhat Cerovac about 150 HVO members being captured, and Croats were being disarmed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, something that puzzled me, and it's something that Judge Antonetti asked you also on Monday, is: How come that on that same day, on the 23rd of March, Mr. Bruno Stojic and Brigadier Petkovic come to the area and that immediately a cease-fire agreement is arranged? How come that's within the day that they could calm down the tensions in that region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day, if Milivoj Petkovic, and I don't remember who else there was with him, they arrived before the conflict had grown larger, so there was still a significant likelihood for the tensions to be reduced. If they had come later, that probably wouldn't have been possible. On the 23rd of March, there was adverse weather, too. That was also one of the reasons why things stopped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, General Petkovic. Do not forget that you are going to testify, so keep your ammunition. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. There is a technical problem. The Prosecutor probably forgot that this was an order and not a visit. One is an order that you can dispatch, and another thing is to arrive in person. So the Prosecutor said "visit," whereas you never mentioned a visit. You said "order." Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could I ask you to take a look at P01911. It's the ECMM report that we have looked at before. Sir, this is a document that we've already looked at on a number of occasions, P01911.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- 01911. This is the ECMM report dated the 16th of April, 1993, and I would like now to draw your attention to paragraph 3 of this report. Do you have it? P01911. I think you have the wrong document. Maybe the usher can help. Now, sir, I'm going to read out a couple of paragraphs from Chapter 3 of this report. Starting at the top: "The clashes that have occurred in the past months have generally followed provocation, and it's the experience of ECMM and some UNPROFOR units that the provocation is usually HVO inspired." Moving to the third paragraph: "Furthermore, the HVO have emphasized Muslim aggression. Any possible material has been used to their advantage. An example is the recently published document seized at gunpoint from the kidnapped chief of the police at Konjic. The document is, in fact, the minutes of a routine BiH municipal --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you mind reading slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: My apologies to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The document is, in fact, the minutes of a routine BiH municipal meeting. The contents are routine and in no way suggest that the military actions should be taken against the HVO, as the HVO might suggest it does." Sir, let me just ask you about this paragraph. Were you aware about this document that was seized from this kidnapped chief of the police in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object to this question because we haven't defined which document was seized from the chief of police in Konjic, and who kidnapped him, when, what this is about. So my request is to lay a foundation for the question first.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'm simply asking whether he knows about this incident, that the Konjic chief was kidnapped. Maybe he doesn't know, and then I'll continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that at the check-point toward Kostajnica, Mr. Jasmin Guska was detained. He was heading for Buturovic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you also know that some documents were seized from him, and did you get a chance of reading these documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which documents these are. I may have read them, but I'm not sure which documents you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's continue reading. The fourth paragraph: "The list of incidents comprising provocation are heavily weighted towards the HVO, and it is considered by monitors in the region that any incident initiated by the BiH follows HVO provocation and not the other way around. The flag issue is another example. The HVO planted their flags all around Gornji Vakuf and were distraught when some went missing." Moving a few paragraphs down: "ECMM observation concludes that HVO provocation is intense, that their explanations for military action contains no truth, and that there must be a clear requirement from Mostar for much of the aggression to take place." Now, sir, would you agree with me that this ECMM report is very outspoken about the HVO provocations towards the ABiH in this region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't receive the full interpretation. Could you repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that the ECMM report that I just read out is very outspoken about the HVO provocations towards the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for my unit, the positions it held, I disagree with the report these people made because I think that no reasonable man would provoke an enemy three times stronger than himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, is it not true that the armed clashes in Konjic on the 23rd of March were mainly the results of HVO provocations against the Muslims in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already spoken my mind. How can someone who is three times outnumbered provoke the other side? I really don't understand these minutes. I can go on to clarify. If we consider the fact that our unit is holding the line toward the JNA and the Serbs in an equal share with the ABiH, that means that our reserve units, and they were very weak and we know how many units the ABiH had, and any provocation of a much stronger enemy would have been madness, and I don't see how it could have happened at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you keep talking about the HVO units within Konjic, but isn't it true that there were also HVO units in the neighbouring municipalities of Prozor and Gornji Vakuf, and that those units were right at the border of Konjic were posing a direct threat to the Muslims in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this is about attacks on Konjic on the 23rd of March.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, correct, and I'm -- what I'm saying is that because of the military threat of the HVO, that there were enormous tensions between the HVO and the ABiH, and that these tensions were as well caused by all the provocations of the HVO within Konjic and outside Konjic. Let's look again -- let's --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it's illogical, and I can only repeat that I don't see how somebody would there provoke somebody so much stronger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you said on several occasions that there were at times tensions between the Muslims and the Croats, and several documents go to that, but that's not the issue. When you found yourself in a situation of tension between two parties, one side is Side A, the other side is Side B, the fact that you create an event or an incident, is that not likely to exacerbate things? In the current climate, if you hoist a flag, whatever flag it may be - this was here the chequerboard flag - was it not likely to cause among the Muslims some kind of reaction? That is a question. You were on the ground. The fact that a chequerboard flag was hoisted was not going to cause an inconvenience to anybody, or did you think that it might cause reactions? And that's the question by the Prosecutor. He asks you whether all this amounted to provocations or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that hoisting a Croatian flag should not bother anybody. Hoisting a flag is one thing, and the affiliation to the people is another thing. Muslims also hoisted their green flags with crescent and the star, and we were not bothered, so I don't see why the chequerboard flag of the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina should have bothered somebody, by the same token.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under Tito's rule, would it happen that on religious festivals, these types of flags could be hoisted, like the chequerboard flag, and would that be normal? I believe that there were religious festivals when flags were hoisted. Maybe I misunderstood, but can you confirm this or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about the former regime and about the JNA. I know that what we had at the time was a uni-party system, and the only flag that could be hoisted was the flag with a five-pointed star, which was the state flag of the Socialist Federative of Republic of Yugoslavia. As for religious events, I don't know whether they were celebrated openly or not, or locally, and in that case people would carry flags of the local population, traditional things that those people have, like their traditional costumes and other symbols.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe just before the break, let's have -- let's continue with the exhibit that we're on, and let's move to Chapter number 4, which is called "Military Activity." I will read out the second, third, and fourth paragraphs: "The BiH forces lack heavy weapons, and when fortifications are levelled, they are left cradling their Kalashnikov rifles, while the HVO retain their transport armour and artillery. The local BiH forces appreciate this disadvantage and can no longer reasonably accept further mediation or compromise in negotiation for peace if it leaves them at such a disadvantage." "The BiH and HVO each recognise the other's strengths and weaknesses. The HVO strength lies in their organisation, resupply, communication, armour and artillery; while the BiH have their backs to the wall and positions in depth." Sir, would you agree with what the ECMM officer has written here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't agree. It is not true that BH Army members did not have artillery, as they call it. If you only remember Sefer Halilovic's order that was carried out by Zejnil Delalic that the artillery from the area of responsibility of Territorial Defence, that Zvekusa should be moved to Igman, those were cannons, Howitzers and mortars, and that was carried out by Zejnil Delalic upon Sefer Halilovic's order. This is just one of the proofs that they did have artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think it says that they did not have artillery. They just said that the HVO had an advantage over the ABiH when it came to artillery. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree. When it comes to Konjic, I believe that they had even more artillery than the HVO members there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, again, if we look at the wider region and if we don't focus just on Konjic, if you look just generally at the ABiH and the HVO in the region Konjic-Jablanica-Prozor-Gornji Vakuf, the wider region, would you agree that the HVO had an artillery advantage over the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say what they had in those areas, but what I had just a minute ago, I know full certain what they had. I can't speculate as to what they had in the territory of Mostar or other areas. I really wouldn't be able to do that. I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with the assessment of the ECMM in paragraph 3, where he says that when it came to cease-fire agreements in this period, and I think, you know, we just discussed the 23 March peace agreement, that such cease-fires would generally be more beneficial to the Bosnian Croats, who were a minority in the region and who were far better organised and equipped with heavy weapons and artillery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said it. It was in our interests to stop all the conflicts in general. And as far as how well we were equipped and how well members of the BH Army were equipped, I believe that they were well equipped and that they were even better equipped than the HVO, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think it's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite. Let's break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe Mr. Karnavas has something to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, Your Honours. Again, hello to everyone. I just wish to point out that today we got the Prosecution's response to the motion on provisional release. We are not seeking --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry to interrupt counsel. We are still in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, okay. Okay. Can we go into closed session, then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May we?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to stay on -- a little longer on the causes for the 23 March clashes. Could I ask you to look at P01698. P01698. This is a BritBat report dated the 22nd of March 1993, and I would be interested in paragraph 5 of the report, which is headed "Gornji Vakuf." Let me read out what the third paragraph under "5. Gornji Vakuf," what it reads. Halfway through the paragraph: "Approximately 40 soldiers wearing 4th Brigade HV badges were sighted in the town -- " I see you're still trying to find the document. Do you have it, Witness? Maybe the usher can help you find it. It's P01698, and I'm interested in paragraph number 5, Witness. And it's a chapter called "Gornji Vakuf." I will read out to you a part of the third paragraph of this chapter: "Approximately 40 soldiers wearing 4th Brigade HV badges were sighted in the town hall carrying new 5.56-millimetre Austrian (sic) assault rifles." "Comment: B Coy noted that there have now been four separate units sighted in Prozor. They are believed to be the following: A, Rama Valley Brigade HVO; B, Jajce Brigade HVO; C, 4th Brigade HV; D, 163rd Brigade HV?" "B Coy comment that these sightings may be one of the reasons why the BiH commander in Gornji Vakuf, Hagic [phoen], was claiming that the HVO were concentrating their forces in Prozor." Comments end. Sir, did you know that HVO and HV forces were concentrating in Prozor on the 22nd of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that. I didn't know that they were concentrating forces there. I never saw a single member of the Croatian Army in the territory of my municipality. I went as far as Mostar, and I never saw people wearing HV insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move to another document, P01747. This is an UNPROFOR report, P01747. UNPROFOR report, and I'm going to read out a section which -- 01747, yes, and I will read out a section. On the English page, it's page number 3, and I think you will have a B/C/S translation of that part at the end. On page 3, under "B. Gornji Vakuf," it reads the following: "The relationship between the Muslims and the Croats appear to have deteriorated during the past seven days. On 21 March, according to BritBat reports, the HVO to the east of Prozor," the area bordering Konjic, "attacked the Muslim village of Here. Following the attack, concentrations of soldiers from both sides were noted in the surrounding villages and fighting was reported from some of these villages. Towards the end of the week, the situation in both Prozor and Gornji Vakuf seem to have improved with both towns returning to their own degree of normality. In retrospect, the majority of the activity in the area appears to have taken place in the villages to the east of Prozor." Now, sir, isn't it correct that the east of Prozor directly borders Konjic, the eastern area of Prozor, and that in fact the village of Here is very close to the Konjic border?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Here, Kute, and Scipe are very close to the borders of Konjic municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a technical question for you. We have an UNPROFOR report on screen. Now, when you were in the field, did you see them in their positions, watching what was happening with their binoculars, taking notes, in order to report that in Here, this and that place, such event happened? According to your recollection, were they really present? Were they canvassing the area correctly? Were they in such a position that they would not be making mistakes when they were reporting the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not observe any such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're saying, I did not see. You didn't see them? They weren't there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They could have been there, but I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were deployed on the field. Any serviceman on the field, you know, is going to observe the situation and try and detect what's going on, check whether the enemy is there, for example. They were neutral, they were not enemies, so why is it that you could not detect them? Were they camouflaged, were they in dug-outs? You're saying that you couldn't see them. That's a bit strange.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't tasked with observing or watching UN members. I dealt with completely different things. I collected intelligence about the enemy and some other things, so I did not pay attention to the things that you just asked me about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You cannot answer. Fine. Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, yes, and I couldn't see them because it's over 20 kilometres. And if you were asking me about Vakuf and Prozor, even with a pair of binoculars from my position, you could not see anything. You couldn't see anything; I couldn't, no other soldier could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could I ask you to look at a document that you have seen also on Monday or Tuesday - I don't remember - P01712. Now, sir, this is a document from the HVO, a special report from the HVO Rama Brigade, dated the 23rd of March, on the situation in Konjic. Do you recall having looked at this document in your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is being asked is a request from the Rama Brigade artillery to open fire at the villages of Kruscica, Studencica and Jasenik, and then on the next page we see that this artillery fire never took place because of an order of Commander Siljeg; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you -- I'm going to show you now a map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the map is in your binder, and I would like to request the assistance of the usher. The map is P11122. It's the last document in the binder. And I would ask the usher to take the map out of the binder and place it on the ELMO. Now, sir, this is an UNPROFOR map, and the Office of the Prosecution has made a few markings on this map in order for everyone to find places more easily. And it also indicates where the various units were stationed. Now, we've been talking here about the village of Here, and what I would like you to do is take a marker and put a circle around the village of Here on this map. Could you please do that for me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And from the report that we just read, there was a request to shell the villages of Kruscica, Studencica and Jasenik. Now in order to assist you, we've placed red lines underneath these villages, but could you please encircle these three villages? So Kruscica, Studencica, and Jasenik. Sorry for the pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you agree with me that these three villages are located not far from the village of Here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with that. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [No interpretation] [Interpretation] Your Honours, what is a relative distance or relative closeness? In the military, there are kilometres. Your Honour Trechsel, what is relative distance? We have 500 such words here, "Relative distance," "relative closeness." For what? For throwing a stone, for throwing a bomb, for a cannon, for a mortar? These are military issues. There are kilometres, yards, so there is length, width, height. I really don't know. I don't know. I have been patiently refraining myself from many reactions. The questions are "far away," "close," "do you see over a hill." What is that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, the witness is a serviceman, just like you are. If he finds out that the question put to him by the Prosecutor creates a problem, he can ask the Prosecutor, Why are you talking about a relative distance? For example. So he can put the question to the Prosecutor. He might not put that question because he is maybe a bit -- feels a bit awkward talking to the Prosecutor. All you have to do is, you know, send a message to your counsel. The counsel will stand up, wait for the witness to finish his answer, and then the counsel will take the floor, say, We might have a problem. What exactly is this notion of relative distance? And the four Judges are also listening and can also wonder about this concept of relative speed or relative distance. Please trust the Judges. You know, they can ask for more information. Everybody can make mistakes; you know, the Prosecutor, the counsel, even Judges, you know, because it's complicated. So don't think that just because one person made a mistake, whether it's the Prosecutor or someone else, this is going to harm your case. Absolutely not. Remember, there are a lot of safe-guards in this procedure. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. First of all, you cannot send a message to Defence counsel, because the guard is not going to give my message to my counsel because that's lowering the security and taking risks. So the guard gives the message to the first lawyer, and that's members of the Pusic team. And for a number of years now, Mr. Pusic's lawyer has been acting as a courier, and I feel embarrassed for that reason. I tried to instruct the guard to take a piece of paper to my own lawyer, but they can't do that. Second of all, it is true that the gentleman is a soldier. How much of a soldier is a different matter, but still it is impressive. But we are hearing the 30th question put to the witness, a question which does not seek to go for the truth. I believe that the Judges will ultimately look at the map and measure. If I didn't believe that, I would stop coming to the courtroom. However, it makes me concerned when I hear that the 30th question of the type has not been interrupted, and those questions are not telling us anything about the real distance, the dates, the number of soldiers. For years now, we have been having I don't know what kind of discussion. It's like us being in medieval ages. We can't go into the field to see whether there is a road or whether there is not a road. We have been dealing with speculations. I believe that the Trial Chamber will finally take some measurements, I believe that, but allow me to say that for three and a half years now, I've been sitting here, and I'm saying I don't mind being convicted if I'm guilty, but this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As far as the transmission of messages is concerned, I had asked the Registry for the accused to be next to their counsels, like they are in the US, for example, and like they are in many democratic countries. As far as security is concerned, I don't think you're going to run away. It seems pretty obvious. But the Registry, for some reason, decided not to allow this. And naively, I thought that they could establish some kind of process in order to make sure that messages could be transmitted easily, but this was not set up. I know that in a courtroom, people are always listening, so I'm sure that Mr. Hocking, our Registrar, is going to be told about this problem quickly, and I hope that he will find a solution. It seems very -- it's incredible to think that the accused cannot have realtime communication with their counsel. There could have been a solution. You could have had a computer, and that way you could just send e-mails to your lawyers. But maybe that's a tall order. So I fully agree with you, because I raised this problem with the Registry already. I concur with you. But maybe we are confronted with administrative inertia, red tape. And the security, it's easy to blame -- to use security as a scapegoat. Now, regarding technical problems that you are raising, remember that we will have some redirect, and the counsels for General Petkovic will be able to ask questions in terms of military issues. And the trial is not over. We know that General Petkovic is going to take the stand, and if huge mistakes have been made, militarily, I'm sure he will correct them. And Judges are there. The Bench is there to check everything. So this is what I had to say. Mr. Bos wants to take the floor, but my fellow Judge has something to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Perhaps I'm saying something which you would have raised; namely, translate what we see into language. This is a map 1:100.000, which means one centimetre on the map equals one kilometre in the terrain. There is a net of vertical-horizontal lines that are one centimetre apart. It is very easy to get a picture of the distances, as I see it. The longest distance is between Here and Jasenik, and that's 14 and a half to 15 kilometres. The shortest is between Kute and Studencica and Kruscica, and that is roughly five kilometres. I don't know what the fuss is about. This is really open and easy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, actually, Your Honour did pretty much take the words out of my mouth. I was going to suggest a lot of this, Mr. Praljak did have a point, and a lot of the trouble would have headed off if a distance was simply put. I do 100 per cent agree, even leaving aside the fact that a village called "Here" is always likely to call confusion on an English transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, the map did have a scale, so I think people could have --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me, but the point is that it's much easier, we then don't have to subsequently look at the map to work out what was actually meant in distance by the rather loose phrase "not far from," which I understand to have been His Honour Judge Trechsel's point, and, well, he made my point for me as well, with respect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Bos, please resume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if we can just stay with the map for a little longer. Now, we just read this report from P1712, in which HVO Konjic is asking artillery assistance from the Rama Brigade. Would you know if these -- so there's a request for the shelling of these three villages that you just marked. From where would the HVO Rama Brigade would have shelled these villages, if it would have happened? Would you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where the artillery positions were at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's -- I'm going to ask you some few more -- to make a few more markings on this map. Yesterday, you've discussed the Boksevica hill, and you were shown a document by the Defence, which was P01887, which discussed the Boksevica hill, and it read something to the effect that whoever holds Boksevica hill had control over almost the entire Neretvica Valley. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you basically confirmed that statement, that Boksevica hill, in fact, did control the whole Neretvica River Valley; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please mark for me the Boksevica hill, put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then could you please indicate what would be referred to as the Neretvica Valley.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicating]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can indicate it with the marker, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just seeing a line. Could you please make a circle around the whole valley.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, is it correct that the HVO controlled the Boksevica hill up until about mid-July 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it controlled all of Boksevica. If you remember the report from the 1st Battalion, it said that there is a communication centre on Boksevica and there are some two or three dozen soldiers on Boksevica. I don't think that there was a need for more soldiers, because at that time there was no conflict with the ABiH. But now things are different because there is a conflict between the ABiH and the HVO, and now this is about taking control of Boksevica hill. Whoever takes it automatically controls the communications centre and the passage through the Neretva Valley -- sorry, Neretvica Valley. And I was also saying yesterday from Papratsko through the Neretva Valley, all this way [indicates]. But the inscription "Boksevica" is only in part. The map only shows the highest peak. But this is the entire area of Boksevica all around it [indicating].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, knowing that Boksevica hill was under the control of the HVO in March and April 1993, would you agree with me that control over this very strategic and very important hill caused, you know -- caused a serious military threat to the ABiH, especially if the HVO had artillery on Boksevica hill?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object to this question because my learned friend stated that the HVO controlled all of Boksevica in March and April 1993, which has not yet been established as a fact in the proceedings. So I would like to ask my colleague to be very precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, I understood the evidence from yesterday to say that - and I think the witness said so - that Boksevica hill was taken over -- that the ABiH took over Boksevica hill by mid-July 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, I would like to remind you of line 1 on page 83: [In English] "Controlled all of Boksevica." [Interpretation] These are the witnesses words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say that what is marked here is only the highest peak of Boksevica, but Rodici, Mrakovo, Mrakove Stijene, all these also belonged to Boksevica. And further on toward Zuglici, all these I mentioned, were controlled by the ABiH all the time. When we speak about Boksevica and which part of it the HVO controlled, then what is meant is only the peak of Boksevica, where the repeater was, the heart of our communications centre. The HVO at no moment in time controlled all of Boksevica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In military technique, you've just gave a detail that was not shown on the map, and I didn't know about it. You say that next to Boksevica hill, there were ABiH units that were positioned. And using your pen, you showed those positions, or you're doing that right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I also say -- I made the point so many times. We've got a couple of references already over the last few minutes to the witness indicating. We see that at line 11 on page 83. We see it again at line 13 on page 83. He did indicate, but what he did was indicate; he wasn't then invited to mark. We saw what he indicated, but it doesn't appear on the transcript. We also now have a number of circles. Some of them are very obviously related to particular places with names, but we've got that large circle which doesn't coincide with the line which the witness already drew as being the valley, and then we got a smaller circle -- or they're not quite circles; they're oblongs. Once again, Your Honour, I do make the point we end up with these maps that are just in a mess from the point of view of future use of them, when we all get back to them even a few minutes, let alone weeks and months and so on, after we have actually been sitting in court, seeing what's happening and what everybody is pointing to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, Mr. Stewart is a stickler for precision, and he's asking you to draw a precise map, so could you put an "A" on the Boksevica hill, where there were 20 to 30 HVO soldiers? Just draw an "A," and this way it will be clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, regarding the valley, can you write in "B," the letter B, and so everybody will know that "B" stands for the valley and "A" for the place where the 20 to 30 HVO soldiers were positioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next to "A," you drew three short lines. They show the ABiH positions. Maybe you could write a "C" there so that if we match this with the transcript, we will see that they correspond to the ABiH positions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... of the witness. I do want that to be very clear. I do accept that there is an implicit criticism in what I said, I don't shrink from that, but it's not directed at the witness at all. He has done exactly what he's been asked to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let us now come to the technical question. There are ABiH units that are listed or shown under "C." They are positioned between Boksevica and Jablanica. Do you agree with this observation that can be seen by anybody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To your knowledge, do you know whether the ABiH units had mortars or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The units of the ABiH had mortars. Where they were deployed, I'm not sure, but I'm positive that they had some here in Ostrozac and Poprazac [phoen] [indicates]. And you asked me yesterday whether it is possible that they had removed their mortars from the line facing the Serbs to this area, you may remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're telling us that you're not totally positive, but there may have been mortars. In the event that they had mortars, could they have fired on Boksevica hill, shown under "A," in order to destroy the 20-odd soldiers that were there, and in so doing in causing or neutralising this threat that the Prosecutor saw in the fact that the 20 soldiers were positioned there? Militarily speaking, it may have been that the military action was to neutralise the HVO positions through mortar fire so as to reduce the capacity to be dangerous. Would a serviceman do that, or would you rather attack with footmen to take the hill? What would be the right military solution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the village of Papratsko and Ostrozac, they were able to open fire on these positions. They could have also sent sabotage units to this village at Boksevica. And in the document that was shown yesterday, it was said that a part -- the part of a unit from Jablanica was sent here to assist here around Mrakovo [indicates], at the foot of Boksevica, so that there was an attack in place on our communications centre on Boksevica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, when we saw the video with the Muderiz unit that was in Jablanica, I guess that when they were in Jablanica, it meant that the ABiH had taken control of the hill shown with letter A. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment when they were receiving the plan of combat activities, the ABiH did not control the Boksevica hill, not fully, so their task was to link up with Here, Kute, and Scipe as soon as possible; that is this direction [indicates]. And here at the foot of Boksevica, they deployed sabotage units. I cannot remember which company or which battalion they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last question. To your knowledge, we see a unit positioned under letter A, these 20 to 30 HVO men. Until when did they stay in that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't mention a precise date, but probably when everybody retreated; that is, in mid-July, probably, because until then the communications centre was in function and we had contact with the 1st Battalion. Later, we lost all contact with the 1st Battalion because the communication centre in Boksevica was down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are saying that the communication centre was down around mid-July, which would mean that the HVO withdrew. So it's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: An observation regarding the transcript. Around page 87, line 1, it is the witness that starts speaking, but it cannot be seen on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We have a few minutes left. Do not forget that we have the Gotovina trial -- oh, no, no, no, they're sitting in Courtroom II today this morning. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let me just recap some of the evidence that we've heard today and which I've showed you today. I've showed you evidence of HVO offensive actions against the ABiH in the neighbouring municipalities of Prozor in October 1992, and in Gornji Vakuf in 1993. I'm sure --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honours. I object to the phrasing "offensive actions."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I've showed you evidence of armed clashes between the Muslims and the Croats in Prozor and Gornji Vakuf. I showed you a UN report which talks about HVO ethnic cleansing of Muslims in Prozor in October 1992. I've showed you an HVO ultimatum document issued to the ABiH on the 15th of January, 1993, also addressed to the Konjic municipality, to submit their command to the HVO Main Staff. And now I just showed you evidence of an HVO attack on the village of Here on the 21st of March, which is located right next to the border of Konjic. With all that in mind, is it still your position that the Muslims -- that there was no reason for the ABiH to feel any threat with regard to HVO aggression in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is still my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move to April, then. And again I would like you to look at Exhibit P01911, the ECMM report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: P01911. It's a document we've looked at on a couple of occasions, and I'm going to read out Chapter 6 to you: "There is no known plan of either side, save for the apparent and declared intent of each side to hold their ground."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you for slowing down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The HVO have declared their intent to implement the Vance-Owen Plan." "However, analysis of political manoeuvre by the HVO, their military build-up, the ground and strategic importance of the region suggests that the HVO wish to implement the Vance-Owen Plan to their advantage." "The HVO make regular radio broadcast ultimatums to the Muslim forces in Herceg-Bosna (never written), yet seldom follow up the ultimatums, suggesting that the concept is to provoke the Muslims into action that can then be used to justify aggression in the name of defence." "Because the Muslims will now bow to the HVO designs, the HVO will have to use force to subdue the region, and indications are that intense military preparation has taken place to this end. Much reinforcement has taken place south-west of," and then there's a place which is not readable, "... from Tomislavgrad." "The HVO need to secure roads into the disputed area, and Muslim factions in Gornji Vakuf, Here, Parsovici, and Konjic dominate all four routes through the region. These four positions have come under concentrated military assault, while villages without strategic importance are left unmolested." Now, sir, this document talks about immense military preparation has taken place to this end. Is it not true that the HVO were preparing for a large military action in the wider region around mid-April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you about the broadcast of these ultimatums. You said that you never saw any written ultimatum, as far as it concerns the 15th of April ultimatum. Did you maybe hear about oral ultimatums being spoken on the radio, or did you ever hear anything about ultimatums around mid-April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never heard in any media a direct ultimatum issued by anybody to anybody else. There was talk in town about some things, but that wasn't the ultimatum, itself. Those were only individual renderings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of talks were in town? Can you be a bit more specific? What was being said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say. I said that I have never seen or heard a direct order, the one that you mentioned to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object on this question. The mode of question, and the previous one, the last one, it is a direct request of the cross-examiner to the witness to speculate. The witness clearly said what he does know or he didn't. He said there were some stories about that, I have heard something in the village. And after that, he is again asked. This is a clear example of speculation. Why do we need the witness to speculate? This is not the evidence, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I completely disagree. He is saying he heard talks, and I'm just asking him to specify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. Mr. Kovacic, there's no need for you to intervene. On line 16, page 90, the witness said, No. So he provided an answer, he answered. So there's no reason for you to rise on your feet. He said that there was no ultimatum through the radio, and now you challenge the Prosecutor. He does his job well, less well. Well, he does his job, anyway. And by saying what you say, you're challenging him. He's doing his job, like you do yours, and the witness is the referee, and he says, No, I don't -- and then he said something. The Prosecutor says he doesn't agree, and we have the text in front of us, and we can see. I can see that there were ultimatums through the radio, but which ones? It's not stated in the document. It could be anything. Let's say, you know, Let's get together, there's a meeting because there's foot-and-mouth disease. Nothing is specific here, so no need to take the floor to say that your learned colleague is manipulating the questions. The Judges are listening, they're attentive. They'll correct as needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I want to clarify. I think there has been perhaps a slight misunderstanding. Your objection is to the question, What did people speak about? And here, what the witness has first said, he never had direct ultimatum, he never knew about the direct ultimatum. We are on page 90, line 20. But then he added, There was talk in town about some things. And the Prosecutor asked him, What kind of talks?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: So the witness had not, before that, said he had no idea what kind of talk it was. That was still open at that moment, so the question was absolutely correct, and the objection must be overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. I wouldn't waste any more time, but please later you can check the transcript. And he exactly refers to the crucial question and answer, and this was my objection. After that, what you referred on page 90, line 22, then Mr. Bos is going again on the same. After the answer of the witness on 91, line 1 -- sorry, on 90, line 22, it was clear. He said there was talk in town about some things, but that wasn't ultimatum, those -- and then it continues some. But I'm sorry, but I think that the objection is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have 40 minutes left, Prosecutor. We shall resume tomorrow. Witness, we shall reconvene, and you'll come here again tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
